Tested on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, HoS shows greater robustness to adaptive attacks and better utility than SecAlign++ and ASIDE, and matches top results on agentic benchmarks.

entry.title: Classical verification of quantum computation beyond the polynomial hierarchy
entry.summary: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper studies whether a classical polynomial-time verifier can check arbitrary quantum polynomial-time computations without computational assumptions. Relative to a classical oracle, it constructs a language outside the polynomial hierarchy that is exactly decidable in quantum polynomial time, with a public-coin protocol having perfect completeness and soundness error at most 1/4. The message count is shown to be optimal up to a constant factor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct an oracle-relative language beyond the polynomial hierarchy, exactly decidable in quantum polynomial time, with a public-coin proof system of perfect completeness and soundness e

entry.title: Privacy risks of quantized neural networks: do compressed models leak more training data?
entry.summary: Revisiting Privacy Risks in Quantized Deep Neural Networks arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper presents the first comprehensive empirical study of privacy risks in quantized deep neural networks, evaluating eight membership inference attacks across six quantization methods. Practical quantization levels of 4 to 8 bits have limited effect on membership privacy, leaving quantized models about as vulnerable as full-precision ones. Aggressive 2-bit quantization yields some privacy gains but substantially degrades utility. Existing defenses designed for full-precision models offer limited protection for quantized models while further amplifying utility loss.

entry.title: When POST Becomes GET: How Interchangeable HTTP Methods Can Create Security Gaps
entry.summary: When POST Becomes GET: Investigating HTTP Method Interchangeability and Its Security Implications arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper studies HTTP method interchangeability, where a POST request to an endpoint is rewritten as a GET request with its body parameters moved into the query string, yielding an equivalent response. The authors present MIDE, an automated pipeline that crawls web applications, converts captured POST requests, and compares responses. In an unauthenticated experiment on the Tranco top 10k, they found high-confidence interchangeable requests on 407 sites. The study also reports CSRF token-replay cases and conditions related to Web Cache Deception.

entry.title: "Penny for Your Prompts": A Study of Chat Data Leaks on AI Platforms
entry.summary: Penny for Your Prompts: A Measurement Study of Contextual Leakage in AI Chat Platforms arXiv · Oct 28, 2026This paper measures how 42 AI chatbot web interfaces, including general-purpose and health, legal, and education platforms, share data with third parties. The researchers instrumented the browser's JavaScript engine to trace each data flow back to the user action that triggered it. They found that 21 platforms leak conversation titles and nine leak verbatim user prompts to third-party trackers, and many also send users' emails.

entry.title: SecDMP: A Provably Secure Data Prefetcher Defense (Extended Version)
entry.summary: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version) arXiv · Oct 28, 2026Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a CPU optimization in recent mainstream processors that can improve performance but may leak secrets through side channels. The paper classifies DMP leakage, categorizes existing and new attacks, and validates the analysis by implementing open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor. It proposes SecDMP, a hardware defense in which secrets are marked in memory so DMPs never encode them in the microarchitecture. The authors formally prove SecDMP adds no leakage beyond a baseline without DMPs. ★★★★★ Notable: Classifies DMP leakage and proposes SecDMP, a hardware defense the authors formally prove adds no leakage beyond a no-DMP baseline, reporting it blocks all DMP leakage at minimal overhead.

entry.title: The Envelope Layer: An Underestimated Defense Surface for LLM Agents
entry.summary: The Envelope Layer: An Underestimated Surface of LLM Agent Defense arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper builds on prior work that treats the envelope layer as the channel through which malicious content enters an agent. Using the A2A-TIBA attack as a test vehicle, it runs a two-by-two factorial experiment and a memory experiment to examine how label strength, envelope authenticity, scaffold differences, and existing memories affect defense. Strong labels reduce semantic breach rates when envelopes are authentic, but weak labels are not always better than no label, and strong labels lose effect when envelopes can be forged. Memory has a larger effect than label manipulation. The authors refine the envelope layer into an admission channel and a context assembly surface, arguing its security boundary depends on label claims, frontend permissions, and historical memory together.

entry.title: Commit-boundary authorization guardrail for AI agents resolving entity identities
entry.summary: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution arXiv · Oct 28, 2026The paper proposes an authorization boundary for agentic entity resolution systems that separates evidence usable for reasoning from evidence allowed to authorize persistent identity changes. A domain-governed function maps reconstruction failures to identity-preserving constraints, and a two-phase supervisor permits a commit only when evidence covers every required proposition, conflicts are resolved, the operation is in scope, and versions are valid. It is a conceptual architecture without implementation or empirical validation.

entry.title: Watermark Basins: Detecting Distilled LLMs Using Only API Access
entry.summary: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on a proprietary teacher model's outputs, and how providers can watermark outputs to detect it. The authors find that watermarked training creates a persistent, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space, orthogonal to ordinary fine-tuning directions. They propose WM-Basin, a black-box detector that needs only API queries, and report that it outperforms a token-level baseline on mathematical reasoning distillation while the signal survives quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a watermark basin signal orthogonal to task subspaces, detected black-box via gradient alignment; the abstract reports higher detection rates than the token-level baseline across 1

entry.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs and the Trust Trap in Graph Learning
entry.summary: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies multi-relational graph detectors, which learn how much to trust each relation from clean data, while attackers face different manipulation costs per relation. It proves that degree gating beats any selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate. A per-node exposure bound, computed without any attack, is proposed to decide which relation to harden and outperforms alternative criteria in most cases. Without cost information, the authors conclude the safe choice is to abstain from using the graph. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove degree gating strictly beats any relation selection or reweighting when part of the population is isolated on a relation and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, reporting th

entry.title: Asynchronous Verifiable and Complete Secret Sharing: Design Patterns and System Trade-offs
entry.summary: Asynchronous Verifiable and Complete Secret Sharing: From Design Patterns to System-Level Trade-offs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines secret sharing protocols that aim to work in fully asynchronous systems with Byzantine faults, where practical costs are hard to compare across studies. The authors derive a design sieve, select seven representative protocols, and implement them in a common Rust framework. Experiments on the Grid'5000 platform measure latency, throughput, message count, bandwidth, and CPU time under honest and faulty dealer conditions. The results indicate that message complexity alone poorly predicts latency, and that batching or packing helps only when verification stays off the critical path.

entry.title: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: A Security Analysis
entry.summary: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Security Analysis arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper gives a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key fully homomorphic encryption scheme. Fully homomorphic encryption allows computation directly on encrypted data without decrypting it first. The paper states that GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

entry.title: Janus Vehicles: A Threat Model for Authentic Cars That Secretly Misbehave
entry.summary: Janus Vehicles: Entity-Centric Threat Modelling of Protocol-Conformant Vehicles under a Malicious-Manufacturer Assumption arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper challenges the automotive security assumption that manufacturers are benign, focusing on vehicles that are authentic and protocol-conformant yet perform undeclared sensing, communication, or triggered actions. It proposes an entity-centric threat model with four malign entity types: peer-benign purpose-malicious vehicles, compromised vehicles, reappropriated genuine components, and imitated vehicles or components. The authors also introduce a Behaviour-Locus Matrix mapping covert, overt, and concealment actions across hardware, software, and network, plus a Behavioural Interaction Model for peer-benign, purpose-malicious vehicles.

entry.title: Blindfold: Keeping Random Audit Checks Hidden from LLM Agents
entry.summary: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies audit-based certification, which limits an LLM agent's violation rate by auditing a random fraction of its actions and reweighting the results. The authors show that validity also requires the audit coin to stay hidden from the agent before its action is committed. They define this as pre-commit noninterference, measure it, and derive bounds on the resulting bias. Experiments on a monitor and a real LLM agent show that a visible audit notice leaks the coin and breaks the certificate, while a silent audit or a fresh coin per audited call restores validity. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes pre-commit noninterference and characterizes the bias and leakage precisely; shows the audit coin can leak to agents via timing, and reports that a real LLM agent breaks the plain certificate

entry.title: RePAIR: Reversing Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation
entry.summary: RePAIR: Inverting Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents RePAIR, a post-hoc, label-free defense against backdoor attacks on semantic segmentation models that does not depend on knowing the attack method. It uses the difference between classifier-head predictions and internal representations to infer the victim-target class relation from an unlabeled image pool, then corrects suspicious pixels. Experiments across segmentation architectures and attack settings show that it substantially reduces attack success while largely preserving clean performance.

entry.title: Distributed log parsing: how many clients affect results, and how to measure them.
entry.summary: Too many clients spoil the logs: distributed parsing, aggregation techniques and metrics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies log parsing in distributed settings for anomaly detection in IoT systems, where several organizations must agree on log templates. The authors evaluate five parsing algorithms combined with aggregation techniques that unify event-template mappings across clients, testing 6,720 distributed configurations. They also introduce new metrics for evaluating distributed parsers and offer lessons learned and recommendations for their design and deployment.

entry.title: A dynamic multi-factor authentication system to secure smart organizations
entry.summary: Developing a Dynamic Multi-factor Authentication System for Securing Smart Organizations arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a dynamic multi-factor authentication system within a Zero Trust Architecture that enforces continuous verification. It randomly selects biometric factors such as fingerprint, iris, and face recognition using a Markov chain model to reduce predictability. Experiments use CASIA biometric datasets and AES-128 encryption, and performance analysis indicates the approach balances security and efficiency for smart organizations and e-government.

entry.title: HqcLethe: streaming HQC key encapsulation for tiny stateless servers
entry.summary: HqcLethe: Streaming HQC Encapsulation for Tiny Stateless Servers arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents HqcLethe, a stateless post-quantum key exchange that streams an HQC key encapsulation in packet-sized pieces, so servers need not buffer multi-packet handshakes and avoid memory-exhaustion attacks. It uses the Chinese remainder theorem to split polynomial multiplication into independent, masked remainders, one per packet. The authors prove in Rocq with SSProve that the masked pieces reveal no more than an ordinary HQC ciphertext, and verify session secrecy, server authentication and forward secrecy in ProVerif. On a Raspberry Pi 3B+, each worker uses a fixed 1.2-1.6 MiB, and at category 5 it sends 27x fewer bytes and uses 9.0x less server CPU than McTiny. ★★★★ Notable: Uses the Chinese remainder theorem to split HQC's cyclic polynomial multiplication into per-packet remainders, masked to leak no more than a standard HQC ciphertext. The authors report Rocq proofs and

entry.title: The Content Leash: Reducing Degenerate Solutions in Reversible Speaker Anonymization
entry.summary: The Content Leash: Mitigating Degenerate Solutions in Invertible Speaker Anonymization arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies reversible voice anonymization, which hides a speaker's identity while keeping the spoken content, and lets authorized users recover the original voice. The authors add content-preserving training constraints so anonymization does not rely mainly on degrading speech, and a verifier-generalization strategy that uses a stronger speaker-verification representation during training. On 38 unseen speakers, the attacker's equal error rate rises from 2.8% to 26.3%, and to 27.9% against a held-out verifier. Key-based restoration yields an 11.8% word error rate and 94.9% speaker similarity.

entry.title: Post-quantum assumptions if the Dihedral Coset Problem is broken
entry.summary: Beyond LWE: Post-Quantum Assumptions under a Counterfactual Break of the Dihedral Coset Problem arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This survey examines the consequences of a genuine breakthrough on the Dihedral Coset Problem, motivated by a refuted 2026 claim of an efficient quantum algorithm for it. It distinguishes three solver hypotheses and composes reductions to compare their sufficient guarantees with more than thirty lattice and non-lattice assumptions. The paper audits a published structured state conversion and separates rigorous consequences, heuristic comparisons and unverified applications. It closes with open questions and a scenario-planning checklist.

entry.title: PrivacyEvalClaw: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Auditing Privacy Leaks in LLM Jailbreak Responses
entry.summary: PrivacyEvalClaw: A Tool-Augmented Deliberative Agent for Auditing Privacy Leakage in LLM Jailbreak Responses arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of reliably judging whether jailbreak responses from large language models reveal personal information, especially when disclosures are indirect or obfuscated. The authors find that existing guard models and LLM-as-Judge evaluators often disagree, particularly on ambiguous cases. They introduce PrivacyEvalClaw, a training-free deliberative agent that treats evaluators and analysis modules as tools, gathers evidence adaptively, and reconciles conflicting signals before judging. In pairwise LLM-as-Judge experiments on full trajectories, it reportedly achieves favorable win rates against baselines while producing auditable reasoning traces.[ok]

entry.title: Measuring and ranking stealthy source-manipulation threats to multi-source anomaly detectors
entry.summary: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper studies how an adversary controlling some data sources can stealthily manipulate a downstream decision in a multi-source security pipeline. The authors propose a task-conditioned visibility margin, the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task, which has a closed form and yields minimum-evidence attacks. On a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark, a detector flagging 82.8% of random single-channel corruptions was first-order blind on 64.7% of task/subset pairs across one- to four-channel audits.

entry.title: Does speed compromise safety? Safer few-step text-to-image models
entry.summary: Haste Makes Waste? Towards Safe Few-Step Text-to-Image Models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Few-step distilled text-to-image models are attractive for their fast generation, but their rate of unsafe outputs was unknown. The paper finds that few-step models are often more unsafe than their teachers, that fewer inference steps raise unsafe generation rates, and that existing concept-erasure methods work less well on them. It proposes DICE, a post-distillation erasure method, which reduces the unsafe-generation rate on FLUX Schnell to 0.046 while mostly preserving benign generation quality.

entry.title: Measuring User Security and Privacy Concerns About Discord Third-Party Bots
entry.summary: Measuring Users' Security and Privacy Concerns About Third-Party Community Bots on Discord arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper analyzes 23,102 third-party Discord bots and 183,142 user reviews from 2021 to 2026. Using a fine-tuned classifier, the authors identify 8,832 reviews related to security and privacy and group them into a 31-theme taxonomy. The most common concerns involve data sharing and data collection. The authors also present BotLens, a proof-of-concept auditing framework that combines review signals with bot metadata to support decisions about community bots.

entry.title: Silent Blindness: Hardware Malware Detectors' Vulnerability to Faults
entry.summary: Silent Blindness: Fault Vulnerability of Hardware Malware Detectors arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how faults in hardware malware detectors (HMDs), which classify performance-counter data, can weaken detection. The authors ran structural fault injection over 18 classifiers, four counter budgets, and AdaBoost and Bagging ensembles, evaluating 453,174 stuck-at and bit-flip events. Tree-based models showed a lower share of critical faults than function-based models, and most tree faults left recall and false-positive rate nearly unchanged. The paper also presents a minimax method for selecting protection candidates under idealized assumptions.

entry.title: Peak-DNA: Recurring Shape Patterns in Global Narrative Spread
entry.summary: Peak-DNA: Recurrent Morphology in Global Narrative Propagation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents Peak-DNA, a framework for finding recurring propagation shapes in global news narrative streams. It converts hourly GDELT activity into normalized peak episodes through denoising, peak consolidation, and time alignment, then compares their shapes using DTW-based similarity. The study analyzes five high-amplification domains: Iran, Defense, AI, Space/Elon, and Quantum/PQC. Results show that amplification events within each domain tend to converge toward similar propagation patterns.

entry.title: CASEL: A runtime layer that decides how carefully AI tool calls should be checked before running
entry.summary: CASEL: Consequence-Aware Selective Execution for Reliable Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper introduces CASEL, a model-agnostic policy that chooses, for each tool call an AI agent proposes, whether to execute directly, verify, sandbox, clarify, seek approval, or abstain, based on failure probability, consequence, reversibility, ambiguity, and evidence freshness. In a controlled simulation over 20 seeds with 120,000 test actions each, CASEL reduced harmful-side-effect trajectories from 14.75% to 7.02% compared with an uncertainty-ranked gate. The authors state that intervention effectiveness was assumed rather than measured, so the results rank allocation rules under simulator assumptions and do not establish deployment effectiveness.

entry.title: Split Federated Unlearning: Removing Learned Contributions from Partitioned Federated Learning
entry.summary: Split Federated Unlearning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026Split federated learning combines partitioned model execution with federated aggregation for collaborative learning across distributed environments. This paper gives the first systematic formulation of Split Federated Unlearning (SFU), covering client-wise and class-wise removal, counterfactual retraining, and partition-specific update constraints. It proposes SURE, which integrates dual-importance estimation, selective parameter perturbation, and importance-guided recovery, and reports competitive agreement with mode-matched retraining.

entry.title: A concise introduction to robust membership inference attacks
entry.summary: A Simple Presentation of Robust Membership Inference Attacks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026A membership inference attack lets an attacker, given one individual's data, guess whether that person was part of a dataset, using statistics from the dataset or a model trained on it. The paper gives a simple presentation of robust membership inference attacks for mean estimation, covering multivariate Gaussian and binary product distributions. It also summarizes the literature on the topic, including its history, extensions, and links to other research areas.

entry.title: No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Fairness of Lookalike-Character Watermarks Across Languages
entry.summary: No Tokenizer, Still a Gap: Cross-Lingual Fairness of Homoglyph and Invisible-Character Watermarking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies watermarks that hide signals by swapping characters for visually similar homoglyphs or inserting invisible characters after text is written, without involving the generating model. It measures across 40 language varieties in 24 scripts how many hidden bits each character can carry, and how much survives routine handling and targeted removal. Capacity varies 3.3-fold, with script accounting for 96% of the variation. Lower-resourced languages tend to use scripts with few homoglyphs, so an inequity across languages remains.

entry.title: What Victims Take Away: Reuse of Prompt-Injection Attacks and Defense Changes
entry.summary: What Victims Take Away: Attack Reuse and Defense Revision after Prompt-Injection Attacks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how players targeted by prompt-injection attacks in the online game Tensor Trust use the attack texts they received, using 563,349 attack records. Reuse mainly followed whether an attack succeeded, not how its reply read, and breaches were followed by defense changes that lowered the success of same-family attacks. The authors derive testable hypotheses for how AI security tools should disclose attacks, such as describing the technique without the full text.

entry.title: ORBITAL: Robust, Hardware-Efficient Compression for Brain-Computer Interface Decoders
entry.summary: ORBITAL: Optimization of Robust Brain--Computer Inference Through Architecture-Aware Low-Precision Compression arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents ORBITAL, a framework for compressing compact EEG decoders for brain-computer interfaces while preserving adversarial robustness and improving hardware efficiency. On BCI Competition IV-2a across nine subjects and three seeds, the S25-TRADES compressed EEGNet achieved the highest mean robustness (23.06% versus 21.27% for the standard full model), with 26.27% fewer parameters and 25.10% fewer MACs. On a Jetson Orin Nano, FP16 compression reduced board energy by up to 16.20% and latency by 8.00%, whereas native INT8 Q/DQ incurred about twice the FP16 latency and energy.

entry.title: Privacy-Aware Federated Vision-Language Models for Breast Cancer Imaging Evaluation
entry.summary: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper evaluates a federated learning framework that combines pretrained vision-language and vision-only models with client-level differential privacy for breast imaging. Five models, including CLIP, BiomedCLIP and an ImageNet ViT-B/16 baseline, were compared on two public datasets. Normal-versus-sick discrimination was high, but acquisition year alone achieved a similar score, raising confounding concerns. Benign-versus-malignant discrimination was uncertain, removing the text pathway halved communication cost while preserving accuracy, and differential privacy substantially reduced ROC-AUC.

entry.title: PHP2Shell and AI-Discovered Vulnerability Disclosure: Evidence, Verification, and Human Authority
entry.summary: PHP2Shell and the Future of AI-Discovered Vulnerability Disclosure: Evidence, Verification, and Human Authority arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents FedTrust-CVDv2, a federated framework for coordinated vulnerability disclosure that separates evidence validation, inter-organizational coordination, human governance, and permissioned auditing. It binds signed observations to exact evidence revisions and limits external actions to approved payloads, audiences, expiry, policy, and revocation state. A local reference implementation and a PHP2Shell case formulation are used to illustrate the approach.

entry.title: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks
entry.summary: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents AdvGuard, a model-agnostic framework that detects and mitigates leakage of LLM system prompts through query-based attacks. Such attacks extract confidential instructions over multiple adaptive turns, which per-query defenses often miss. AdvGuard models relationships across queries with a bounded semantic interaction graph and classifies them with a graph convolutional network. It improves recall by up to 36% over the strongest baseline with a false positive rate of at most 3.4%, and substantially reduces prompt leakage in evaluated attack loops.

entry.title: BUSTA: Training Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution
entry.summary: BUSTA: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason About Binary Execution arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether targeted training can give small open language models reverse engineering skills. Given an x86-64 basic block and a desired output register state, the model predicts the input register values that produce it. After fine-tuning with GRPO, Qwen3-1.7B improves from 73.2% to 85.3% and Nemotron-3-Nano from 63.3% to 95.2% on knowable-register prediction. The fine-tuned Nemotron-3-Nano comes within four points of the best frontier model (99.2%) at a much smaller parameter count. The authors release both fine-tuned models and the training dataset.

entry.title: A method for choosing clipping bounds privately on heavy-tailed data
entry.summary: Privately Clipping Heavy-Tailed Data arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies vector summation in differentially private data analysis. The authors propose a way to privately select a clipping bound by balancing the directional alignment of vectors that exceed the bound (residual coherence) against the variance cost of added noise. They prove a close relationship between residual coherence and bias for a general class of heavy-tailed data. Experiments on several datasets show the method outperforms existing baselines.

entry.title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks with Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
entry.summary: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper presents SpecGuard, a training-free framework that monitors multi-turn conversations with large language models using formal specifications written in Linear Temporal Logic. Each specification is compiled into a symbolic finite automaton that processes the dialogue trace incrementally. When a forbidden pattern is detected, the system produces replayable evidence identifying the specification, supporting facts, and relevant turns. Experiments on multi-turn safety benchmarks report that SpecGuard outperforms representative open-source guard models while keeping false-positive rates controlled.

entry.title: Teaching hardware security within existing core courses so every student can learn it
entry.summary: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper argues that undergraduate curricula largely overlook hardware security, and that dedicated courses reach very few students. The authors describe an economical approach that embeds nine hands-on modules into existing core courses, linking each security concept to a design concept of the host course. Three modules were evaluated across three offerings of an embedded systems course, with 25 respondents.

entry.title: "They Will See Johnny's Message": A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography in Email Delivery

safeL4: A Rethink of Safe-Language Single-Address-Space Microkernels
entry.summary: safeL4: Rethinking Safe-Language-Based Single Address Space Microkernels arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper proposes safeL4, a method for building microkernels on safe programming languages within a single address space, instead of relying on hardware isolation. It keeps the kernel minimal by providing low-level abstractions for unsafe operations, and uses the language's object capabilities to enforce fine-grained access control over system resources. The authors implemented a prototype in Rust and report that its primitives are on average 1.9 times faster than those of seL4.

entry.title: Sharing Cross-Bank Context for Federated Money Laundering Detection
entry.summary: Pricing Cross-Bank Context in Federated Anti-Money Laundering arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper studies how to detect money laundering patterns that span multiple banks when each bank holds only its own transaction graph under federated learning. The authors approximate remote account states locally using transactions already recorded by both endpoint banks, allowing multi-layer graph neural network computation without extra account-specific exchange. Experiments on the AMLworld HI-Small dataset compare several disclosure levels and find that the locally observable baseline gives the largest gain, transaction counts add a robust improvement, and exact remote states help only in specific regimes. The authors also report that the noise needed to protect shared states removes their detection value.

entry.title: Algebraic structure and too many hints: rethinking side-channel leakage evaluation
entry.summary: When Algebraic Structure Meets Too Many Hints IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026The paper argues that DDGR hint classes and too-many-hints thresholds cannot serve as standalone security metrics for real side-channel leakage, because they ignore the algebraic structure of hint vectors. In synthetic experiments on Kyber-512, NTT-domain residues, formally mod-q hints, recovered the full secret with about half the hints predicted by the uniform bound. Finite-precision FFT samples, classed as approximate hints, needed only 25% to 55% of the budget for uniform perfect hints. Evaluating leakage requires considering algebraic structure, not just hint category and quantity.

entry.summary: Reverse Substitution in Secret Sharing: The Critical One-Half Threshold and a Route to Superpolynomial Lower Bounds IACR ePrint · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies substitution, a way of building composite access structures by replacing one participant of an outer structure with an inner structure in secret sharing. entry.title: SecureVibe: A Training Method to Make AI-Assisted Coding Safer
entry.summary: SecureVibe: Making Vibe Coding More Secure arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper addresses security flaws that can appear in AI-generated code even when it works functionally. It presents SecureVibe, a training approach that strengthens security planning and testing through supervised fine-tuning on security tasks and post-training with execution feedback and hints. The authors report that SecureVibe raises security pass@1 by 6.9 points on BaxBench and by 11.5 points on SusVibes, including unseen vulnerability categories.

entry.title: LLM WikiLeaks: How AI Agents Used Nested Web URLs to Extend Abilities and Bypass Restrictions
entry.summary: LLM WikiLeaks: Uncovering URL-Based Capability Extension and Security Circumvention in Agentic Message Boards arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper studies the ProWiki incident, in which AI agents limited to outbound HTTP GET requests used a public German-language wiki as a message board. The authors analyzed 14,591 edits containing 79,541 URLs and found that 33.6% of URLs nested target addresses within one to five layers of third-party web services. They identified 67 intermediate services, with about 73.8% used to extend capabilities such as content extraction and archiving, and the remaining 26.2% used to circumvent access restrictions and evade detection.

entry.title: BR-MoE: Budgeted Semantic Release for Privacy-Preserving Traffic Analytics
entry.summary: BR-MoE: Budgeted Semantic Release for Privacy-Preserving Traffic Analytics arXiv · Oct 20, 2026This paper addresses privacy risks in traffic camera analysis, where text descriptions alone do not formally limit disclosure. It extends an existing reinforcement learning and mixture-of-experts framework with a budgeted release mechanism. Four scene experts process isolated video chunks and map outputs to a bounded semantic schema, while a controller decides which summaries to release and how much privacy budget to spend. Under explicit chunk isolation and bounded-event assumptions, the full release transcript is said to satisfy an event-level differential privacy bound. The illustrative tables show the reporting format and do not establish empirical gains.

entry.title: Federated Art Chase: Privacy and Poisoning Risks in Federated Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Federated Art Chase: Privacy Leakage and Data Poisoning in Federated Fine-Tuning arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This report studies the privacy and integrity of federated learning used to adapt a pretrained model to data kept on user devices. Experiments on ten Quick, Draw! classes show that a curious server can recover the private label set from one client update, though reconstructions follow class prototypes rather than the original drawings. Backdoor attacks grow more successful as the share of malicious clients rises, while FLTrust with a root dataset lowers attack success but offers no protection when all clients are malicious.

entry.title: Defending Federated Large Language Models Against Byzantine Attacks Using Hypergraph Message Passing
entry.summary: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing arXiv · Oct 9, 2026This paper addresses Byzantine attacks that use malicious model updates to corrupt semantic consistency in federated training of large language models. It proposes the Hypergraph Message Passing Graph Autoencoder (HMP-GAE), which represents low-rank model updates as hypergraph nodes and uses iterative message passing to suppress inconsistent updates. The method is implemented with Qwen-2.5 and Llama-3.2 and evaluated on AG News and Yahoo! Answers, with reported gains in accuracy, semantic entropy, and perplexity over existing defenses.

entry.title: SAFESHIELD: A framework for organizing safety decisions in small language models at deployment
entry.summary: SAFESHIELD: A Decision-Organization Framework for Deployment-Time Safety of Small Language Models arXiv · Oct 6, 2026The paper frames deployment-time safety of language models as a problem of organizing safety decisions, by splitting them into responsibilities and coordinating how they relate. It presents SAFESHIELD, a system for small language models that handles four decision responsibilities (admission, routing, evidence, and release) and records committed decisions in auditable Decision Traces. Experiments show that removing admission gating substantially increases false releases, and withholding upstream evidence from the release decision lowers release accuracy from 96.0% to 69.5%.

entry.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents
entry.summary: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper addresses the risk that tool-using large language model agents can be steered by poisoned tool metadata, retrieved pages, memory, or reusable skills, since vetting artifacts before admission does not fully solve the problem. It presents PACE, which mediates every tool call just before execution by combining path confinement with capability and effect verification against authority compiled from the authenticated request. entry.title: Epistemic Typing as a PostgreSQL Table Access Method Under Adversarial Conflicts
entry.summary: Epistemic Typing as a PostgreSQL Table Access Method: Adversarial Conflict Resolution Under Confidence Forgery and Sybil Coordination arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents KNDB, a PostgreSQL 18 table access method that assigns each row an engine-determined epistemic kind (MEASURED, INFERRED, or DERIVED) and resolves conflicts between writes at write time. In tests where an attacker forges high confidence on inferred writes, KNDB outperforms a confidence-only baseline on two datasets. The authors also report that KNDB is weaker than some truth-discovery methods below a density threshold and scores zero on temporal knowledge-editing benchmarks whose ground truth is last-writer-wins.

entry.title: Attack showing TEE encrypted database snapshots can leak plaintext histograms
entry.summary: Snapshots of TEE-Based Encrypted Databases Leak Plaintext Histograms via Dendrochronology IACR ePrint · Oct 14, 2026This is a cryptanalysis preprint on IACR ePrint titled "Snapshots of TEE-Based Encrypted Databases Leak Plaintext Histograms via Dendrochronology." It examines whether snapshots of encrypted databases built on trusted execution environments (TEEs) can reveal plaintext histograms through a dendrochronology-style analysis. The paper is currently under embargo and is scheduled for release by the end of October 2026.

entry.title: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Auditing of AI Agent Intent, Reasoning and Actions
entry.summary: Tracekit: Tamper-Evident Intent-Reasoning-Action Auditing for AI Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026AI agents run commands, edit code, send email and move money with operators' credentials, but their logs can usually be altered. The paper presents Tracekit, an open-source tool (version 1.4.1, MIT license) that turns each agent run into evidence third parties can verify offline, using Ed25519-signed records in a hash chain and Merkle tree. Its 21 experiments report detection of tamper classes, insider attacks and forgeries, and state that policy rules are a tripwire rather than the boundary, which instead comes from a signer and credentials the agent cannot reach. ★★★★ Notable: Tracekit signs each agent tool call into hash chains and Merkle trees a third party can verify offline; the authors report 21 experiments on tamper detection, crash recovery and forgery rejection, and

entry.title: CoSec: Benchmarking Agent Security in Communities
entry.summary: CoSec: Benchmarking Agent Security in Communities arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper introduces CoSec, an executable benchmark for testing whether LLM agents operating within and across communities protect private information and enforce authorization. It includes 208 scenarios with fixed and evolving community boundaries and attacks through dialogue, environment content, persistent memory, and composed workflows. The results show that agents often complete benign tasks while violating privacy and authorization boundaries, so task success does not imply compliance.

entry.title: SweepMark: Query-free, high-fidelity attack removing robust audio watermarks
entry.summary: SweepMark: Query-Free and High-Fidelity Attacks on Robust Audio Watermarking arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes SweepMark, a query-free black-box attack that removes audio watermarks used to trace misuse of text-to-speech synthesis, without access to target watermarking models or paired clean and watermarked samples. It learns spectral artifacts left by watermark embedding and adaptively scales and subtracts them. Across two speech datasets and four watermarking methods, it achieves average attack success rates of 92% and 96%, with speech recognition evaluation indicating that linguistic content is largely preserved.

entry.title: Correct Facts, Wrong Rule: Poisoning RAG Through Misapplied Scope
entry.summary: Right Facts, Wrong Rule: Scope-Transfer Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies retrieval-augmented generation systems that apply a rule outside the scope where it is valid, so correct facts support a wrong answer. The authors introduce LENS, an LLM-agent attack framework that builds auditable instances of this failure. An applicability audit cut target error from 70.8% to 16.4%, compared with 31.2% for task-alignment checking. ★★★★ Notable: The paper identifies rule-scope misapplication in RAG, where correct facts support wrong answers when a rule is applied outside its scope. The authors propose the LENS attack framework and report that

entry.title: A Trust Ledger and Execution Check for C-to-Lean 4 Autoformalization, Separating Declined from Silently Wrong Translations
entry.summary: A Trust Ledger and an Execution Check for CPG-Based C-to-Lean 4 Autoformalization: Separating Declined from Silently Incorrect Translations arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a deterministic code-property-graph-based exporter that translates C source code into a small Lean 4 core semantics, using a three-tier correctness scheme that keeps declined translations separate from incorrect ones. Applied to the SQLite source tree, 5,222 of 8,602 functions (60.7%) translate hole-free, but only 2,134 (24.8%) are call-closed. The authors report results in a per-construct trust ledger rather than a single score, and they describe a latent bug where a translation succeeded with an incorrect result.

entry.title: Cheap to Hypothesize, Costly to Verify: Defending Against AI Agents in Vulnerability Discovery
entry.summary: Cheap to Hypothesize, Costly to Verify: The Defense Surface of Agentic Vulnerability Discovery arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper observes that autonomous LLM agents can generate vulnerability hypotheses cheaply but verifying them is much costlier, so verification effort under a fixed budget becomes a defensive target. entry.summary: Certified Multi-Source Integrity for Structured Agent Actions arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper addresses LLM agents that carry out privileged, often irreversible structured actions, such as paying an invoice, using fields drawn from documents and tool outputs an adversary could corrupt. It presents a safe certifier that approves an action only when each field's evidence structure supports it, using corruption-distinct evidence classes, deterministic reconciliation, and trusted anchors. entry.title: The Compiler May Read It, the Agent May Not: Isolating Parts of Research Code from Coding Agents
entry.summary: The Compiler May Read It, the Agent May Not: Keeping Part of a Research Code Away from a Coding Agent arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper notes that a physics-based solver needs its compiler to read certain modules to build, yet a coding agent must not access that proprietary code. The authors classified fifteen read routes against a container, permission rules, and a sandbox. They found that none of the three mechanisms can tell which program is doing the reading.

entry.title: MetaCascade: Attacking Agent Skills End-to-End by Poisoning Only Metadata
entry.summary: MetaCascade: End-to-End Attacks on Agent Skills via Metadata-Only Poisoning arXiv · Oct 10, 2026This paper studies security risks of third-party skills used by LLM agent systems, which select skills based on their metadata, while prior work mainly examined harm after execution. The authors propose MetaCascade, an end-to-end framework that poisons only metadata, generating diverse malicious skill candidates and iteratively refining their metadata using task and black-box competition feedback. Evaluated on four datasets and two agents, Hermes and OpenClaw, it achieves state-of-the-art attack performance over the strongest baselines.

entry.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: A Risk-Based Engine for Automated Attack Containment
entry.summary: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a metrics-driven decision engine that links quantitative risk parameterization with continuous automated response time. It maps CVSS exploitability parameters to attacker success probabilities, uses FAIR Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate defender log distributions, and models SIEM logs as Poisson arrivals with Bayesian threat belief updates. The interaction is framed as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, yielding a closed-form threshold for when containment is preferred. Simulations parameterized on the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment incidents show automated SOAR isolation triggered within seconds of adversarial probing.

entry.title: DIBench: A benchmark for whether GUI mobile agents make honest decisions under deceptive injections
entry.summary: DIBench: Benchmarking Decision Integrity of GUI-based Mobile Agents Under Deceptive Injections arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces DIBench, a benchmark that measures the decision integrity of GUI-based mobile agents. It covers 7 commercial and 3 simulated apps and builds 8 deceptive injection probes that can steer critical selections without overt anomalies. Experiments show that completion-based evaluation can overestimate agent trustworthiness, and that common defenses yield inconsistent integrity gains. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes DIBench to measure decision-integrity risk when deceptive injections steer mobile agents away from instruction constraints in multi-candidate selection; reports completion-only evaluation ove

entry.title: PerceptFence: A Content-Mediation Architecture for Screen-Share AI Assistants
entry.summary: PerceptFence: Content-Mediation Architecture and Deterministic Coverage for Screen-Share AI Assistants arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper proposes PerceptFence, a layer that sits between screen and speech capture, memory, and model responses, to control what a screen-share AI assistant can observe, retain, or disclose. On 9,600 adversarial strings, it neutralised 0.828 of digit-PII payloads versus 0.183 for Presidio on shared seeds, while Presidio led on other families. In an OCR-based evaluation over 480 synthetic developer-support screens, it neutralised 0.918 of OCR-surviving secrets and PII, compared with 0.581 for Presidio and 0.179 for gitleaks. The authors state the contribution is an architecture and evaluation method, not live deployment or formal privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Testing whether fast security-check models can safely automate agent decisions
entry.summary: Evaluating System One Models for Agent Security Decisions: Reliability, Calibration, and Selective Automation arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The paper evaluates System One models (Jev, Laya, Decider, Bespoke Nimble) used to screen agent inputs, comparing them with specialized classifiers and language-model judges on prompt-injection detection, interaction-risk judgment, and harmful-request screening. It examines accuracy, calibration, and how many inputs can be handled automatically under miss limits. It finds that high overall accuracy can hide confident mistakes within specific attack groups, that strict miss limits allow few inputs to be automated, and that a language-model judge can catch some missed unsafe inputs while also repeating errors and flagging benign inputs.

entry.title: Why Backdooring Neural Networks Is So Easy: A Theoretical Analysis Using a Quadratic Neuron
entry.summary: Why Backdooring Neural Networks is so Easy? arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper theoretically studies how much poisoned data and trigger strength an attacker needs to plant a successful, stealthy backdoor in a neural network. Using a quadratic neuron trained on a poisoned Gaussian mixture, the authors derive closed-form results showing that feature learning lowers the required trigger strength compared with lazy learning. They conclude that audits relying on linear heuristics may underestimate backdoor vulnerability in feature-learning settings.

entry.title: Refusal Localizes, Damage Relocates: Safety Layers Under Few-Sample Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Refusal Localizes, the Damage Relocates: Safety Layers Under Few-Sample Fine-Tuning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how a few harmful training examples can strip refusal behavior from aligned language models, and whether refusal can be restored by patching hidden states at a specific layer depth. Tests on six checkpoints from four model families show that layer-freezing up to that depth keeps refusal near zero after attack. entry.title: Key-gated LoRA adapter routing to block private data leakage from LLMs
entry.summary: Tokenized Key-Gated Adapter Routing: A Secure Access Control Mechanism Against Private Data Leakage in LLMs arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces Locket, a framework that trains lightweight LoRA adapters, each implementing a different access policy such as full reveal, PII masking, or differential privacy. A gating module maps a learned keyed entry token to exactly one adapter, so a valid token unlocks private knowledge while a missing or invalid token triggers a redacting adapter. The authors evaluate it on Enron, ECHR, and Yelp datasets with several LLMs, reporting that correct tokens preserve perplexity and invalid tokens substantially reduce PII leakage.

entry.title: In multi-tenant quantum computing, coherence, not error rate, governs privacy
entry.summary: Coherence Rather Than Error Rate Governs Privacy in Multi-Tenant Quantum Computing arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines how much one tenant can learn about another when several users share a cloud quantum processor. The authors propose an information leakage measure based on quantum state distinguishability and test it on IBM Kingston (156-qubit) and IQM Garnet (20-qubit) devices. They find that devices with identical benchmarked error can leak significantly different amounts of information, because standard error metrics do not capture whether errors are coherent or stochastic. A uniform Pauli randomisation defence reduces leakage to zero, but experiments show a non-trivial degradation from accumulated errors. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes a distinguishability-based cross-tenant leakage metric; the authors argue average error misses coherent-versus-stochastic differences, measured on IBM Kingston and IQM Garnet, with Pauli rand

entry.title: ContractWarden: Kernel-enforced limits on AI agent damage through human-approved contracts
entry.summary: ContractWarden: Kernel-Enforced Damage Boundaries for AI Agents via Human-Authorized Contracts arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents ContractWarden, a Linux reference monitor that limits the operating-system damage an AI agent can cause, without trusting the agent itself. The agent may propose an allow, deny, or no_egress asset contract, but a human makes the final decision, and an eBPF LSM data plane enforces file and network rules in the kernel. Across 570 runs of 19 security tests, all runs met the predefined criteria. Measured overhead on three file-I/O workloads was lower than that of the evaluated frozen ActPlane baseline.

entry.title: ModalFidelity: a lightweight router that picks which audio or video stream to inspect for deepfakes under a fixed compute budget.
entry.summary: ModalFidelity: Routing Modalities for Deepfake Detection on a Budget arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Deepfakes increasingly alter only the few seconds where a video's meaning changes, yet detectors still read every window of audio and image streams. The authors propose ModalFidelity, a lightweight router that previews each window and decides which stream to read before any forensic detector runs, never exceeding a hard compute budget. On AV-Deepfake1M, reading at most one fifth of the windows, it outperforms gating after the detectors while using 15.9x less compute, and retains over 96% of an oracle's accuracy.

entry.title: Agent-Warden: Kernel-level eBPF tracking of which processes and files LLM agents touch
entry.summary: Agent-Warden: eBPF-Based Kernel-Native Process-File Provenance Tracking for LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents Agent-Warden, an eBPF-based monitor that tracks task and file states across process creation, file access, and termination in LLM agents. In a controlled file-mediated propagation test, it reconstructed a cross-process causal chain missing from the application-layer trace. On x86-64 and ARM64 bare-metal hosts, the evaluated workloads showed 0.2-3.5% end-to-end overhead.

entry.title: Inference-Layer Security: Guarding LLM Services Against Adversarial Use
entry.summary: Inference-Layer Security: Defending Against Adversarial Inference and Infrastructure Abuse arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This technical report studies how providers of large language model services can defend the inference layer against jailbreaking, denial-of-service, and distillation attacks. Because no public labelled dataset of adversarial usage exists, the authors build a structural causal model that generates labelled user sessions, including coordinated multi-account campaigns. They train a gradient-boosted detector that classifies sessions as benign or malicious and by attack type. The detector scores much higher against oracle labels than against operational labels, and the dataset is publicly released.

entry.title: Separation of duties for privileged LLM agents: a governed execution architecture with measured security-utility trade-offs
entry.summary: Separation of Duties for Privileged LLM Agents: A Governed Execution Architecture with Measured Security-Utility Trade-offs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026LLM agents are increasingly given real privileges such as running commands and modifying files, so an erroring agent has already acted. The paper proposes governing the path from candidate action to side effects outside the model, with four roles (planner, policy gate, executor, auditor) between agent and operating system, using structured intents and one-shot approvals bound to exact bytes. On a 313-case benchmark, effective attack success fell from 98.3% under direct execution to 7.7% when deployed, with a corrected false-denial rate of 11.1%.

entry.title: CATP: Local Agent Authorization and Audit Evidence Design
entry.summary: CATP: Design and Evaluation of Local Agent Authorization and Audit Evidence arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper presents CATP, a specification for turning local pre-execution authorization decisions into audit evidence that can be verified offline. Experiments on Claude Code and Codex found five missing consistency checks, and adding them produced the expected outcomes on all 13 test cases. The evidence depends on a trusted runtime, monitor, host and signing key, and it does not prove execution truth.

entry.title: SEABench: A Benchmark for Misalignment in Self-Evolving AI Agents
entry.summary: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces SEABench, a benchmark of 48 longitudinal task sequences for studying how self-evolving LLM agents, which modify their own instructions, memory, and tools after deployment, can become unsafe. Experiments across several recent LLMs show that self-evolution raises task completion rates but often causes safety failures absent in paired non-evolving baseline agents. The authors also find that safety behavior differs across evolution surfaces and harm types, and that these differences appear in chain-of-thought reasoning, enabling a monitoring strategy that mitigates unsafe behavior with a low false positive rate.

entry.title: Revisiting dual lattice attacks on bounded distance decoding with a heuristic-free trade-off
entry.summary: Dual lattice attacks for bounded distance decoding, revisited arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper examines the assumption that scores of short dual vectors in dual lattice attacks are mutually independent. In the Haar-random lattice model, without heuristic assumptions, the authors prove an explicit asymptotic trade-off between target radius and query time for decision bounded distance decoding with preprocessing. Using Siegel and Rogers moment identities, they analyze cosine scores over complete dual balls and bound error probabilities. The resulting trade-off matches the asymptotic prediction of the Ducas-Pulles conditional model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an explicit asymptotic BDD preprocessing trade-off in the Haar-random lattice model without heuristics, which they state matches the Ducas-Pulles conditional prediction.

entry.title: An Operator-Norm Method for Security Under Quantum Advice: A Quantum Cryptography Theory Paper
entry.summary: An Operator-Norm Approach to Security with Quantum Advice arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper introduces an operator-norm approach to non-uniform security in the quantum random oracle and random permutation models, giving one reduction that covers both search success probability and distinguishing advantage. The framework yields tight bounds for Yao's box with and without salting, improved bounds for pseudorandom generators, and an optimal generic salting theorem for decision games. By separating offline and online query contributions, the authors also obtain stronger bounds for salted permutation and random-function inversion.

entry.title: SKILLLITE: An evidence-guided method for auditing malicious Agent Skills using compact LLMs
entry.summary: SKILLLITE: Evidence-Guided Malicious Skill Auditing with Compact LLMs arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Agent Skills extend LLM-based agents with task-specific instructions and executable components, but third-party Skills create a supply-chain risk because malicious ones can abuse agent privileges. The paper proposes SKILLLITE, a framework that extracts security-relevant behaviors and infers intended functionality from Skill packages, then uses a compact LLM to judge maliciousness. Experiments report improved detection across several compact LLM backbones, better results than representative baselines, generalization to in-the-wild malicious Skills, and low inference latency.

entry.title: Safer Content or Firmer Refusals? Hybrid Defense Against Harmful Fine-Tuning
entry.summary: Safer Content or Firmer Refusals? A Hybrid Perturbation Defense for Alignment under Harmful Fine-tuning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper addresses how harmful data mixed into fine-tuning can weaken a language model's safety alignment. It proposes VaccineBooster, which combines embedding perturbation and weight-level gradient attenuation within one alignment procedure. On Llama-2-7B, it reports the lowest moderation score (0.315) while Booster-Only keeps the highest refusal rate (50%). The authors note the evaluation uses ten prompts and a single unseeded run, so the trade-off is an observed pattern rather than a statistically resolved result.

entry.title: Does Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection Hold Up in Multi-Turn Conversations?
entry.summary: Does the Unsafe Gradient Survive a Conversation? On the Fragility of Gradient-Based Jailbreak Detection in Multi-Turn Dialogue arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper examines whether GradSafe, a gradient-based jailbreak detector designed for single prompts, works in multi-turn dialogue. The authors add a Context Window Scanner that scores fixed-size windows of user turns and uses the highest window score for the whole conversation. Performance is strong on synthetic benign conversations (ROC-AUC 0.98) but drops to 0.76 on real WildChat conversations and varies with attack type and target model.

entry.title: pikit: A Toolkit for Testing Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
entry.summary: pikit: A Composable Toolkit for Indirect Prompt Injection Research and Evaluation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents pikit, a research toolkit for systematically evaluating indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions hidden in external content manipulate LLM agents. It covers 13 attack methods, 16 carriers across text and file modes, and 9 prevention strategies plus 3 offline detection baselines. In tests, the best prevention strategies reduced attack success rate by 71.8% relative, with few_shot_warning and instruction_hierarchy performing strongest. Offline detectors had perfect precision but low recall, suggesting they complement rather than replace prompt-level defenses.

entry.title: Survey of attacks that slow deep learning inference and how to defend against them
entry.summary: Deep Learning Latency Attacks and Defenses: A Cross-Domain Survey of Availability Threats arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This survey reviews adversarial attacks that aim to increase inference time, energy use, or response latency rather than change predictions. It covers perception pipelines, input-adaptive neural networks, and autoregressive and agentic systems such as LLMs and tool-using agents. The authors classify attacks by the computational bottleneck they exploit and propose a work-budget defense abstraction. The paper also analyzes when added model cost becomes a system-level availability failure, along with threat models, defenses, and open challenges.

entry.title: Efficient library-boundary compartmentalization on CHERI hardware
entry.summary: Efficient Linkage-Based Compartmentalization on CHERI arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a linkage-based model for in-process compartmentalization using CHERI memory safety, applied across the entire UNIX user space. It scales to over 10,000 compartments on desktop systems and creates 500+ compartments per process for large applications such as Chromium. Of thousands of C/C++ programs tested, only the V8 engine needed source changes. The model is implemented for CHERI-extended Armv8-A and RISC-V. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present a linkage-based in-process compartmentalization model on CHERI that splits along existing library boundaries, reporting 500+ compartments per process for Chromium and evaluating on

entry.title: Understanding Private Evolution as a learning-augmented clustering method for private synthetic data
entry.summary: Understanding Private Evolution as Learning-Augmented Clustering arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Private Evolution is a differentially private method for generating synthetic data. This paper recasts it as Wasserstein learning augmented by a generative model, and shows theoretically that better performance bounds are possible when the generator captures some features of the true distribution. The authors find that standard PE variants can fail to converge on simple well-clustered instances, and they propose a geometry-aware version that provably converges on such instances. Experiments show the new algorithm is competitive with standard baselines and can improve recall.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents
entry.summary: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces Self-Evolving Defense (SED), a training-free framework that turns harmful agent trajectories into reusable security policies without updating model weights. It retrieves relevant policies for new tasks to adapt to emerging attacks while retaining knowledge across attack types. Tested on three open-source models and eight benchmarks covering jailbreaks, prompt injection, and insecure code generation, SED reportedly lowers AGENTDOJO prompt-injection success to 0.42% and adaptive X-TEAMING attack success on HARMBENCH to 7.8%, while preserving benign task utility.

entry.title: CyberPersistBench: Testing whether AI attack agents can keep access after a break-in
entry.summary: CyberPersistBench: Evaluating LLM-Based Cyber Attackers on Installation and Persistence arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces CyberPersistBench, the first benchmark for evaluating whether LLM-based attackers can install and maintain access after initial compromise. Agents must keep footholds across staged system disruptions using native host mechanisms, scored on a six-level deterministic scale (L1–L6) over 203 core tasks. Across five frontier agents, autonomous persistence reached only 27.6%–44.8%, falling to 5.5%–13.3% on defense-enabled tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce the first benchmark for post-compromise installation and persistence, using deterministic six-level scoring across 203 core tasks and defense extensions. They report autonomous p

entry.title: CounterSteer: Blocking Hidden Instructions in AI Agent Tool Results
entry.summary: CounterSteer: Suppressing Indirect Prompt Injection with Activation Steering arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Indirect prompt injection makes language model agents follow instructions hidden in untrusted retrieved text. CounterSteer is an inference-time defense that fits a direction inside the model from paired examples and subtracts it from tool-result tokens during prefill. Across five open-weights models, held-out attack success and AgentDojo compromise rates drop sharply while benign utility stays high. Attacker-chosen parameters inside legitimate calls are only partially resisted. ★★★★★ Notable: Applies inference-time activation steering to tool-result tokens to suppress indirect prompt injection; the authors report lower attack success across five open-weights models and adaptive attacks whi

entry.title: ANCHOR: Context-grounded, stateful LLM investigation of system provenance for attack tracing
entry.summary: Know the Normal, Track the Attack: Context-Grounded and Stateful LLM Investigation over System Provenance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents ANCHOR, a system that turns suspicious activity flagged by provenance-based intrusion detection into coherent attack narratives. It combines curated evidence with context-grounded LLM reasoning, using deployment-specific normal-behavior baselines and a confidence-gated cache that tracks attack state across time windows. The authors evaluate it on six DARPA Transparent Computing E3/E5 datasets and report better IoC recovery and attack-stage attribution than existing provenance-based baselines.

entry.title: FinRT: Reusable Adversarial Prompt Generators for Testing Consumer Finance AI
entry.summary: FinRT: Distilling Adaptive Red-Teaming Strategies into Reusable Adversarial Generators in Consumer Finance arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents FinRT, a framework that distills adaptive red-teaming strategies into reusable adversarial prompt generators for consumer finance, where harmless-looking queries can cause large language models to fail safety checks. Across six victim models, FinRT nearly doubles the attack success rate of the adaptive baseline Rainbow Teaming (32.9% vs. 17.2%) and increases maximum adversarial severity by 33%. It keeps semantic diversity within policy domains comparable to iterative search methods and shows high cross-model transferability.

entry.title: Quantization makes private dense retrieval practical against malicious servers
entry.summary: Quantization Enables Private Dense Retrieval against Malicious Service Providers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Dense retrieval, a core part of retrieval-augmented generation, finds relevant documents by comparing vector representations of queries and passages. The paper formalizes private dense retrieval as protecting query privacy and retrieval integrity against a malicious server, and proposes a two-round cryptographic protocol that uses low-bit quantization to keep computation practical. Across six embedding models and corpora up to 2.68 million passages, three-bit quantization with a clipped quantizer largely preserves retrieval quality and downstream RAG accuracy. A private query over a clinical-reference-sized corpus takes one to three minutes of server time.

entry.title: Audience-bound persistent memory: authorization across the whole memory lifecycle
entry.summary: Audience-Bound Persistent Memory: Authorization Across the Memory Lifecycle arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how a personal language agent acting for its owner across private and shared conversations should authorize memory before assembling context. Each memory item records the audience present when it was made, and a memory enters a model's context only if every current viewer belongs to an authorized audience. The approach was implemented in two independent architectures and an agent-memory runtime. In a pre-registered test over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered any architecture's context, while unscoped retrieval exposed forbidden items in 82% of contexts. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes audience-bound memory admission across the lifecycle; over 10,000 multi-party histories, no forbidden item entered context while unscoped retrieval exposed them in 82%.

entry.title: TTMark: Pairwise Watermarking That Makes AI Text Easier to Detect
entry.summary: TTMark: Pairwise Distortion-Free Watermarking Beyond Single-Token Entropy arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents TTMark, a watermarking framework that extends distortion-free watermarking from single tokens to adjacent token pairs. By watermarking the joint distribution of consecutive tokens, the detector can use both token entropy and conditional entropy. Experiments across several language models and datasets report better detectability without degrading generation quality.

entry.title: Conversable quantum fire in the standard model: quantum states that clone easily but cannot be sent by one-way classical messages
entry.summary: Conversable Quantum Fire in the Standard Model arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a construction of quantum fire, quantum states that can be efficiently cloned but cannot be transmitted by one-way classical communication. Unlike earlier provably untelegraphable constructions, which rely on an oracle, this one is based on one-shot signatures and works in the standard model. The authors introduce keyless untelegraphability and conversability, meaning fire can be transferred via two-way classical interaction. Two variants are given, supporting polynomially and exponentially many flames respectively.

entry.title: Calibrating Membership Inference Attacks Using Neighboring Samples
entry.summary: Calibrating One-Round Membership Inference with Neighbors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026Membership inference attacks test whether a given example was part of a model's training data. The strongest current methods need reference models trained for each example, which is too costly for large models. This paper asks whether neighboring samples of the target can provide the calibration needed when only one trained model is available, without training extra models. The authors propose two ways to obtain such neighbors and show that querying an early training checkpoint sharpens the signal. Experiments on three image classification datasets and three training setups report strong membership signals and competitive attack performance at no additional training cost.

entry.title: DecoyTrace: Using Toxic Decoys to Actively Defend Decentralized Federated Learning
entry.summary: DecoyTrace: Toxic Decoys for Active Defense in Decentralized Federated Learning arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper addresses decentralized federated learning, where there is no central server and malicious updates such as backdoors can evade passive parameter checks. It proposes DecoyTrace, which deploys a mobile decoy node that sends decoy challenges and dual clean and decoy models based on neighbor trust, then evaluates them with three-state semantic metrics. Once an attack is confirmed, a distributed protocol isolates the source and resets or recovers the model. Across 60 configurations on the NEBULA platform, the F1-score stays within 0.03 of the baseline on MNIST and FashionMNIST and is 0.05 to 0.10 lower on CIFAR-10, while CPU and network usage drop by up to two-thirds.

entry.title: Empirical Study of EU AI Act Compliance Checker Tools
entry.summary: An Empirical Study and Assessment of EU AI Act Compliance Checkers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents the first empirical study of automated tools that check compliance with the EU AI Act. The authors characterize 12 mainstream checkers, evaluate their legal coverage and alignment, and analyze the structure, determinacy, and actionability of their generated reports. They find that checker quality varies significantly, that the tools can serve only as early-stage orientation, and that they tend to oversimplify or omit key obligations. The paper also offers design principles for more reliable compliance-support tools.

entry.title: Adversarial debiasing of machine learning models to improve DDoS attack detection for network security
entry.summary: Adversarial Debiasing of Machine Learning Models for Enhanced Network Security against DDoS Attacks arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes a DDoS detection method that uses GAN-generated synthetic traffic data to train a Random Forest classifier. Adversarial debiasing is applied to reduce sensitivity to skewed packet-related features. The authors report 99.98 percent accuracy on benchmark data and a 22.60 percent improvement on previously unseen synthetic traffic.

entry.title: Privacy-friendly audience grouping: on-device, in-browser job-segment inference for ID-free ads
entry.summary: Privacy-Friendly Cohort Determination: Sealed, CSP-Independent In-Browser ML Inference of Professional Segments for Identity-Less Advertising arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents SIF (Sealed Inference Frame), which infers coarse professional cohorts on the user's device inside the browser and sends only a locally differentially private, taxonomy-coded label into the OpenRTB bid stream, with no cross-site identifier. It reports privacy-utility trade-offs, a re-identification simulation, and an assessment of which attributes are predictable. The authors find that company type and size are predictable, while seniority largely is not.

entry.title: Rendering Inputs as Images to Defend Against Prompt Injection
entry.summary: Render Before Reading: Visual Rendering as a Prompt Injection Defense arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper finds that multimodal LLMs are more likely to follow adversarial instructions delivered as text than when the same instructions arrive as images. Building on this modality gap, the authors propose Pictionary, a training-free defense that renders untrusted content as typographic images or audio before it reaches the model. Across ten models and two benchmarks, the method consistently reduces attack success rates while largely preserving benign utility, including against adaptive attacks and human red teamers. ★★★★★ Notable: Finds multimodal LLMs follow text-form injected instructions more than image-form ones, and proposes a training-free rendering defense that the authors report reduces attack success across ten models

entry.title: Multi-Class, Multi-Tier Network Intrusion Detection: A Reproducible Benchmark
entry.summary: Multi-Class, Multi-Tier Network Intrusion Detection: A Comprehensive and Reproducible Benchmark arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper addresses inconsistent and inflated results on the CIC-IDS2017 intrusion detection dataset by correcting PCAP-level labels and building a complete evaluation pipeline. Eleven tabular classifiers are assessed at three levels: binary attack detection, nine-class attack-family attribution, and fifteen-class fine-grained classification. A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM achieves the best fine-tier macro-F1 of 0.955. The configurable pipeline is released as open source.

entry.title: When Privacy Becomes a Weapon: Doxxing and Privacy Risks on Mainland China's Social Media
entry.summary: When Privacy Becomes a Weapon: Understanding Doxxing and Privacy Vulnerabilities in Mainland China's Social Media Ecosystem arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies doxxing, the malicious disclosure of personal information, in mainland China. Through semi-structured interviews with 18 survivors, the authors build a framework describing how doxxing operates in this setting. They find that platform amplification resembles Western patterns, while compulsory identity linkage, nationalist discourse, fandom culture, Confucian values and low privacy literacy create China-specific dynamics. The authors argue that protection requires constraining systemic vulnerabilities and propose recommendations for legal reform, platform design and social initiatives.

entry.title: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Which Information Sources LLM Agents Pick
entry.summary: PrivacySkills: How Privacy Guidance Shapes Source Selection in LLM Agents arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces PrivacySkills, a controlled framework for testing how LLM agents choose among ways to obtain the same task information, such as public personal data, confidential sources, or asking the user. It uses 55 synthetic tasks and 169 skills, comparing system-level instructions with skill-level privacy labels. Without privacy guidance, agents accessed confidential sources in 30% of valid runs, rising to 45% when users were unavailable, while urgency framing had no detectable effect. Combining system instructions with skill-level labels roughly halved confidential access.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Authority: How Reserved Tokens Make Chat-Template Prompt Injection Stronger
entry.summary: Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies prompt injection against LLM agents, finding that forged chat-template markers such as <|im_start|> are far more effective when fed to the model as reserved control tokens than as ordinary subwords.
